title: Bharti Hexacom Ltd - 544162 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Bharti Hexacom FY26 revenue grew 9.4% and EBITDAaL 17.9%, with Q4 revenue at Rs 2,414 Crores (+2.3% QoQ) and EBITDAaL margin of 47.9%.
summary.overview: Bharti Hexacom reported strong FY26 operating leverage, with EBITDAaL margin up 3.4 points to 47.6% and a record 395,000 net homes adds. Q4 revenue grew 2.3% sequentially to Rs 2,414 Crores, while ARPU of Rs 252 was dented by two fewer days and was about Rs 257-258 on an EDB basis. Management flagged handset price rises, lower international roaming and 5G pack consumption as ARPU headwinds, and a Rs 4,000 Crore-range regulatory provision was booked on a changed interpretation of an existing issue. The call was largely a joint Airtel-Hexacom webinar; Hexacom questions focused on lagging mobile growth versus Airtel, FWA versus fiber strategy, and payout.

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 operating free cash flow (EBITDAaL minus capex)

segments.name: Mobile
segments.commentary: Ended Q4 with 28.8 million mobile customers; net adds about 370,000 and smartphone adds about 478,000, the highest in four quarters. Management said the ARPU gap to Airtel has narrowed but Hexacom lags Airtel on FY26 revenue growth (8.3% vs close to 12%).

segments.name: Homes and office
segments.commentary: Record net adds of 148,000 in Q4 and 395,000 for FY26; FY26 homes and office revenue grew 51%. Q4 homes revenue rose about 21% sequentially, helped by FWA expansion to new pin codes, FTTH deepening and IPTV rollout.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given; management said it does not provide guidance and that Hexacom remains committed to progressively increasing dividend payout.
ARPU headwinds expected to persist from lower international roaming, handset price rises and 5G consumption packs; management said there are no red flags on ARPU.
Management expects Hexacom to stay competitive and look for ways to grow faster, including new convergence offers; smartphone upgrades could see some stress.
Hexacom will not give up on homes acquisition; in difficult terrain FWA is used to reach homes where fiber is costly, with fiber-first where available.
capex_capacity: Q4 capex was Rs 586 Crores, described as acceleration as planned.
FY26 capex directed to 5G densification, network modernization and homes and IPTV growth.
Management noted that Hexacom's growth is restricted to mobile and FTTH, which is fully funded, with fewer growth engines available compared to the parent.
demand_pricing: Smartphone upgrades and feature-phone-to-smartphone shift face pressure from rising handset prices; management said FWA connection costs have risen versus fiber in the last three to four months.
Competitive market; management described the ARPU headwinds as similar to other operators, citing lower international roaming and unlimited 5G packs that break the price ladder.
Homes ARPU on new adds is slightly lower than the traditional base, but acquisition ARPU has not declined materially, per the parent's commentary.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Hexacom mobile revenue growth (8.3%) lagged Airtel (close to 12%), and should it accelerate?
qa_highlights.answer: Soumen Ray said Hexacom is underpenetrated in its two circles and the ARPU gap has closed; postpaid and international roaming differences and smartphone upgrade stress may cause some lag, and convergence offers are being launched.

qa_highlights.question: Should Hexacom have a sharper payout ratio given limited growth engines and funded capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said dividend moved from Rs 3-4 to Rs 10-18 per share and it remains committed to a progressively rising payout, while growth engines available to the parent are not open to Hexacom.

qa_highlights.question: Could homes growth slow due to chipset and memory cost issues affecting FWA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FWA remains useful for reaching homes in difficult terrain such as the North East, and it will not give up on home acquisition, pivoting to fiber where available.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the ARPU shortfall beyond international roaming?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 5G pack adoption that breaks the price ladder, handset price increases pressuring 2G to 4G upgrades, and lower roaming; the quarter-average ARPU is not a red flag per management.

qa_highlights.question: Should homes subscriber additions continue at the current pace?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined forward-looking guidance but said the objective is to keep growing homes and there is no fundamental reason to ease efforts, though competition exists.

qa_highlights.question: What does the regulatory charge in Q4 relate to and is it new demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not new; an existing matter was re-interpreted with auditors and the audit committee and a provision was taken under prudent accounting, with no specifics disclosed.

risks_watch: ARPU trajectory with handset price increases, lower international roaming and 5G unlimited packs; Q4 ARPU was Rs 252 reported.
Homes momentum if chipset and memory costs keep FWA more expensive and push the company toward slower fiber rollout in difficult terrain.
Regulatory provision booked in Q4 on a changed interpretation of an existing matter; amount not disclosed in the call.
Mobile growth gap versus Airtel (8.3% vs close to 12% revenue growth in FY26) and whether it narrows.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 operating leverage and homes growth, but cautious on ARPU and handset-driven headwinds; management avoided guidance and deflected competitor comparisons.
key_quotes: Revenues and EBITDAaL growth came in at about 9.4% and 17.9% respectively.
We have increased the dividend payout significantly and we have been committed that we will be looking at a progressively increasing dividend payout and we continue to remain on that.
I would say it is competitive, it is not lagging the market and we continue to look at opportunities as to how to grow faster.

growth.why: No formal guidance was given; management declined to guide on revenue, offering only a continued progressive dividend payout (Rs 18/share FY26 vs Rs 10) and expecting ARPU headwinds to persist, with growth relying on record homes net adds (148k in Q4, 395k FY26) and mobile smartphone adds, without specific capacity or order numbers behind it.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY26 EBITDAaL margin rose 3.4 points to 47.6% and Q4 margin was 47.9%, but ARPU headwinds and rising FWA and handset costs could offset operating leverage, and management did not guide on margins.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or store capacity was discussed; capex is directed to 5G densification, network modernization and homes/IPTV growth, which is fully funded and does not signal new capacity coming live, with Q4 capex at Rs 586 Crores described as on plan.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Record homes net adds of 148k in Q4 and 395k in FY26 with homes revenue up 51%, plus mobile net adds of about 370k in Q4 and smartphone adds of about 478k, the highest in four quarters; management says there is no fundamental reason to ease homes acquisition.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure was disclosed and management said Hexacom's growth is restricted to mobile and FTTH, which is fully funded, so no new capex programme or board-approved expansion was flagged.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or margin guidance exists to raise, and management said ARPU headwinds are expected to persist while mobile revenue growth trails Airtel at 8.3% vs close to 12% in FY26.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management gave no formal guidance, and flagged ARPU headwinds from lower international roaming, handset price rises and 5G packs (Q4 ARPU Rs 252, about Rs 257-258 on EDB basis), plus FWA connection costs up over the last three to four months.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said convergence offers are being launched to grow faster, and IPTV rollout and FWA expansion to new pin codes are under way, though no specific product dates were given.

rows.label: Rs 4,000 Crore-range regulatory provision on changed interpretation
rows.when: Q4 FY26 booked; cash and P&L impact over coming quarters unc
rows.why: Provision booked in Q4 on a re-interpreted existing matter with amount not disclosed beyond the Rs 4,000 Crore range, so further charges or a payout could follow.

rows.label: Progressively rising dividend payout
rows.why: FY26 dividend raised to Rs 18 per share from Rs 10 and management reiterated a progressive payout, with FY26 operating free cash flow at Rs 2,935 Crores and net debt about Rs 2,000 Crores.

rows.label: ARPU pressure from handset prices and 5G packs
rows.why: Q4 ARPU Rs 252 (about Rs 257-258 EDB) was hit by handset price rises, lower international roaming and unlimited 5G packs that break the price ladder, though management says there is no red flag.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 operating leverage, homes growth and the rising dividend, but cautious on ARPU, handset-driven upgrade stress and FWA cost increases; analysts pushed on mobile growth lagging Airtel (8.3% vs close to 12%), the payout ratio, and the nature of the regulatory provision.
